newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Act leader lodges complaint about three MPs.
newsitem.headline: NZ Act leader lodges complaint about three MPs.

text.p: Act New Zealand leader Richard Prebble said on Thursday he had lodged complaints with parliament's speaker about the behaviour of three New Zealand First MPs during Wednesday night's fracas in parliament.
Prebble told Reuters he had witnessed the later stages of the incident, in which it is alleged Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters pushed and argued with National backbencher John Banks.
Peters denied in a radio interview that he had manhandled Banks. Later, in parliament, he offered him an unreserved apology, acknowledging the two had had a dispute which "clearly upset" Banks.
Prebble said he had lodged complaints about the actions of Peters, Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare and Associate Education Minister Brian Donnelly.
"They looked like tow truck operators," Prebble said, describing their treatment of Banks.
